cards.title: Hide the logprobs
cards.what: Many APIs return the probability of every candidate token (logprobs). That is a gift to a thief: instead of one answer per question, the student learns the teacher's whole belief at every word. This is classic Hinton-style soft-label distillation.
cards.how: Attacker: Qwen3-0.6B (same tokenizer as the teacher), the same 1,500 harvested facts, trained once on text only and once with top-20 logprobs (KL loss).

example.context: Ted tells Skyler that he hasn't said a word to anyone and that he told the authorities he

cards.result: with logprobs 0% vs text only –. Hiding logprobs costs honest users nothing.

cards.title: Rate limits & query budgets
cards.what: A student only knows what it was shown. Per-account, per-IP and per-device limits (device fingerprinting, as in my LeakCheck page) cap how much a thief can harvest before paying a lot or getting noticed.
cards.how: The same attacker trained on the first 100 / 300 / 700 / 1,500 facts it managed to harvest.
cards.result: accuracy tracks the budget almost linearly, so whoever controls the budget controls the copy.

cards.title: Extraction detection
cards.what: Thieves don't ask like fans. Fans ask about Walt, Jesse and Saul and come back to favorites; a harvester systematically walks the long tail (every minor character, every location) because it needs coverage.
cards.how: Logistic regression over a sliding window of 20 queries: distinct-page ratio, long-tail share, timing. Tested on 300 simulated sessions of each kind (simulated traffic, not real users).

sessions.label: Real fan (asks about main characters, thinks between questions)
Harvester script (fast, walks the whole wiki)

cards.result: humans flagged 0.0%; harvesters 100.0% (median query 20); stealthy harvesters 100.0% (median query 20). Timing tricks don't help, coverage gives them away.

cards.title: Watermark the answers
cards.what: The teacher slightly prefers a secret, context-dependent "green" half of the vocabulary at every token (Kirchenbauer et al. 2023). Readers can't see it; statistics can. A student trained on those answers inherits the bias, so the copy is "radioactive" (Sander et al. 2024).
cards.how: γ = 0.25, δ = 4, the green list is seeded by the previous token. The detector below runs in your browser with the same Qwen tokenizer and secret key. Paste any text.

cards.title: Canary facts
cards.what: The protected API sprinkles a few invented, harmless facts into answers about obscure topics (only a harvester asks about those). If a competitor's model "knows" your made-up code names, it learned from you.
cards.how: None canaries like "(Archive note: the Nippy file is catalogued under the code name Velvet Quokka.)", each on a long-tail fact.
cards.result: stolen student repeats None/None canaries; clean student 0/20. Accuracy is untouched (–), so this is evidence, not a block.

cards.title: Poison flagged sessions
cards.what: Once the detector is confident, don't block (that tells the thief to rotate accounts). Keep answering with subtly wrong names and the copy learns garbage.
cards.how: After the stealthy attacker is flagged (query ≈20), every answer has its names swapped for other names from the show.
cards.result: stolen student drops to – (from 30%) and confidently says wrong names. Risk: a false positive poisons a real user, so it is only used at high confidence.

cards.title: Hide the reasoning
cards.what: Frontier APIs now hide raw chain-of-thought and return only a summary, partly because reasoning traces are the most valuable distillation data. Here the "reasoning" is one extra sentence of context per answer.
cards.how: Attacker trained on answer + explanation (open API) vs answer only (reasoning hidden), same 1,500 facts.

cards.title: Antidistillation sampling
cards.what: Change how the teacher picks words: among the words the teacher itself finds good, prefer the ones a typical student finds hardest to learn. The answer stays right for people but becomes a worse training signal. Simplified version of Savani et al. 2025.
cards.how: Inside the teacher's top-p 0.9 nucleus, re-rank tokens by teacher log-prob − λ·(proxy student log-prob), λ = 1, with Qwen3-0.6B as proxy.
